content.equation:
Creatinine Clearance (Clcr)
Note: A maximum of 125 mL/minute is used for Clcr. Calculation uses actual body weight to calculate for Clcr, therefore, in obese patients (and possibly patients with ascites)
creatinine clearance may be significantly overestimated. Some clinicians may prefer to use an adjusted body weight in such cases [eg, IBW + 0.4 (ABW - IBW)]. Patients with
estimated Clcr ≥60 mL/minute and actual weight not >130% of IBW may be candidates for once daily dosing. Use clinical judgment.
Cockcroft-Gault Method:
Note: This equation has not been updated for use with serum creatinine methods traceable to IDMS. Use with IDMS-traceable serum creatinine methods may overestimate renal
function; use with caution.
Males: Clcr = [(140 - Age) x Weight] / (72 x Creatinine)
Females: Clcr = [(140 - Age) x Weight] / [(72 x Creatinine)] x 0.85
Clcr = creatinine clearance; calculated in mL/minute
Age is input in years
Weight is input in kg
Creatinine is input in mg/dL
Jelliffe Method:
Note: This equation has not been updated for use with serum creatinine methods traceable to IDMS. Use with IDMS-traceable serum creatinine methods may overestimate renal
function; use with caution.
Males: Clcr = {98 - [0.8 x (Age - 20)]} / (Creatinine)
Females: Clcr = Use above equation, then multiply result by 0.9
Clcr = creatinine clearance; calculated in mL/minute/1.73 m2
Age is input in years
Creatinine is input in mg/dL
Bedside Schwartz Method (pediatrics; ages 1-16 years):
Clcr = (0.413 X Height) / Creatinine
Clcr = creatinine clearance; calculated in mL/minute/1.73 m2
Height (length) is input in cm
Creatinine is input in mg/dL
Traub-Johnson Method (pediatrics; ages 1-18 years):
Note: This equation has not been updated for use with serum creatinine methods traceable to IDMS. Use with IDMS-traceable serum creatinine methods may overestimate renal
function; use with caution.
Clcr = (0.48 x Height) / (Creatinine)
Clcr = creatinine clearance; calculated in mL/minute/1.73 m2
Height (length) is input in cm
Creatinine is input in mg/dL
Elimination Rate Constant (Ke)
Ke = (0.00293 x Clcr) + 0.014 (Bauer, 1999)
Weight Factor (WF) This may be actual body weight, ideal body weight (IBW), or adjusted body weight (ABW):
Ideal Body Weight (IBW):
Children:
IBW = [(height2 x 1.65)] ÷ 1000
IBW = ideal body weight in kg
Height measured in cm
Note: Intended for children <18 years with height ≤60 inches (152 cm)
Adults:
Male: IBW = 50 + [2.3 x (height - 60)]
Female: IBW = 45.5 + [2.3 x (height - 60)]
IBW = ideal body weight in kg
Height measured in inches
Adjusted Body Weight (ABW):
ABW = IBW + [0.4 x (weight - IBW)]
WF = weight (if weight < IBW)
WF = IBW (if IBW < weight < 130% of IBW) normal
WF = ABW (if weight > 130% of IBW)
Volume of Distribution (Vd)
Vd = 0.15 L/kg, 0.25 L/kg, 0.3 L/kg, 0.35 L/kg, or 0.50 L/kg (whichever selected) x WF
WF = weight factor in kg
Half-Life (t)
t = 0.693 ÷ Ke
Ke = elimination rate constant (hour-1)
Suggested Loading Dose (LD)
LD = Cdp x Vd
Cdp = desired peak
Vd = volume of distribution
Note: Suggested dose rounding: Amikacin rounded to the nearest 25 mg; gentamicin/tobramycin rounded to the nearest 10 mg.
Suggested Interval (tau)
tau = [ln(Cdp ÷ Cdtr) ÷ Ke] + 0.5
Cdp = desired peak
Cdtr = desired trough
Ke = elimination rate constant
Note: Suggested dosing interval rounded to 8, 12, 18, 24, 36, 48, 72 hours.
Suggested Maintenance Dose (MD)
MD = 0.5 x Ke x Vd x Cdp x [1 - e(-Ke x tau) ] ÷ [1 - e(-Ke x 0.5)]
Ke = elimination rate constant
Vd = volume of distribution in L
Cdp = desired peak in mg/L
tau = suggested dosing interval
tau = suggested dosing interval
Note: Suggested dose rounding: Amikacin rounded to the nearest 25 mg; gentamicin/tobramycin rounded to the nearest 10 mg.
Predicted Peak at Steady State (Cpp)
Cpp = [(MD ÷ (0.5 x Ke x Vd)) x (l - e-Ke x 0.5)] ÷ l - e(-Ke x tau)
MD = suggested maintenance dose in mg
Ke = elimination rate constant
Vd = volume of distribution in L
tau = suggested interval time in hours
Note: Calculation is based on an infusion time of 30 minutes and drawing level 30 minutes after the infusion. Some institutions may have different infusion times or policies
for drawing the peak; therefore, drawn peak may differ from predicted peak.
Use clinical judgment.
Predicted Trough at Steady State (Cptr)
Cptr = Cpp x e[-Ke x (tau - 0.5)]
Cpp = predicted peak at steady state
Ke = elimination rate constant
tau = suggested interval time in hours

content.instructions: To perform a calculation, enter the required variables. Once all the inputs are entered, click the "Calculate" button to perform the calculation. Any time an input variable is adjusted, the "Calculate" button must be clicked to populate the new output. To start over, click the "Reset" button to clear all values and begin the calculation again. Aminoglycosides are antibiotics commonly used to treat serious enterococcal and gram-negative bacterial infections. They distribute well into synovial, peritoneal, ascitic, and pleural fluids, but poorly into CNS and the vitreous humor of eye. They are eliminated rapidly by the kidneys. Many factors go into aminoglycoside dosing including a patient's age, weight, creatinine clearance, severity of infection, and other disease states. Impaired renal function and increased age can decrease clearance, whereas fever, cystic fibrosis and young age can increase clearance of aminoglycosides. Heart failure, obesity, and ascites can increase volume of distribution. These calculations are only estimates and clinical judgment must be used. Usual desired peak serum concentrations: 1. Amikacin: 15-40 mcg/mL 2. Gentamicin and tobramycin: 4-10 mcg/mL (Note: In patients with suspected gram-negative pneumonia, the peak should be high enough to provide a Cmax:MIC ratio of at least 10:1). Usual desired trough serum concentrations: 1. Amikacin: 1-8 mcg/mL 2. Gentamicin and tobramycin: 0.5-2 mcg/mL Peak and trough serum concentrations can be obtained after the third dose. The peak should be drawn 30 minutes after the 30-minute infusion and the trough immediately before the next dose. Additional serum concentrations can be drawn every 7 days, unless there is a lack of clinical improvement or changes in renal function, in which case, more frequent monitoring may be required.
